description: Seed the 49 missing crops into the cultivos_cultivo table and populate 8 weeks of PrecioSemanal for each new crop. This is the data foundation — FEAT-002 depends on these records existing in DB.
steps: 1. Create apps/cultivos/management/__init__.py and apps/cultivos/management/commands/__init__.py if they do not already exist.

2. Create apps/cultivos/management/commands/seed_cultivos_completo.py as a Django management command (BaseCommand subclass). It must define a list of all 49 new crops with all Cultivo model fields (nombre, categoria, clima, ph_min, ph_max, humedad_min, humedad_max, altitud_min, altitud_max, temperatura_min, temperatura_max, conductividad_min, conductividad_max, nitrogeno_min, nitrogeno_max, fosforo_min, fosforo_max, potasio_min, potasio_max, icono, descripcion, nombre_dane, activo=True). Use update_or_create keyed on 'nombre' so it is idempotent. Full list of 49 crops is in the plan file at .agents/tasks/plan-cultivos-91.md Step 1. Use the descriptive defaults by category (see plan). Print count of created vs updated.

3. Create apps/sipsa/management/commands/seed_sipsa_completo.py. It must: iterate over the 49 new crop names; for each, resolve the Cultivo object with Cultivo.objects.filter(nombre=nombre).first() — create a minimal Cultivo if still not found (should not happen after step 2); generate 8 weekly PrecioSemanal records using the same _lunes_hace_n_semanas/_label helpers from seed_sipsa.py; use prices from the table in plan-cultivos-91.md Step 2 with ±3% weekly variation; use get_or_create keyed on (cultivo, fecha_semana) for idempotency. Set precio_local = round(precio_kg * 0.97, 2). Print total new records created.
4. Run both commands in order: python manage.py seed_cultivos_completo, then python manage.py seed_sipsa_completo.
5. Record the final counts in this FEAT's findings field.
